entries.action: Iran sanctions landed and were absorbed; the du and AD Ports dates are unchanged
entries.rationale: Monday's Bessent announcement was 'Operation Economic Outcast' - roughly 60 entities, vessels and individuals designated across the UAE, Hong Kong, China, Singapore, Switzerland and Europe, with an explicit secondary-sanctions threat. Three UAE names were designated: Unique Oasis Shipping Services, Target Horizon Shipping and Good Luck Shipping - shipping and bunkering intermediaries, NOT banks, sovereigns or listed blue chips. The design was deliberately calibrated: major Chinese banks were spared and no UAE financial institution was designated. The bourses absorbed it rather than breaking. Two things to carry forward: this is explicitly a first tranche with more promised, so a later designation naming a UAE bank or a listed entity would flip the read-across hard; and there is precedent for the UAE regulator force-closing BOTH exchanges - it did so on March 2 and 3 this year after Iranian strikes - which is the single highest-impact tail risk over the du rebalance (Aug 31) and AD Ports tender (Sept 15) windows. NEW DETAIL on du: the MSCI deletions are in the SMALL CAP tier, not Standard - Taaleem Holdings and Deyaar Development both exit at the same Aug 31 close that du enters, so the DFM gets offsetting passive selling on the identical date. Still no published broker estimate of du's inflow exists; the Etisalat precedent of $360-460m is an analogy, not a du number, and must not be quoted as one. AD Ports: nothing new since Aug 21. The offer document still awaits final written SCA approval and the board circular recommending for or against has not been issued - minorities are being asked to tender into an offer their own board has not yet endorsed, which is part of what the ~3.6% spread is paying for.

entries.action: digital assets named a sanctionable Iranian sector - a structural headline risk for the crypto book
entries.rationale: Monday's 'Operation Economic Outcast' did something that reaches the crypto side of this book, not just the UAE side: it designated DIGITAL ASSETS as a sanctionable sector of the Iranian economy under EO 13902 for the first time - one of five sectoral determinations alongside technology, gold, aviation and shipping - and OFAC listed specific crypto wallet addresses tied to the IRGC-Qods Force. UAE entities were named too: Tiany Technology Limited (DMCC Dubai) and Ivan Obukhov, a UAE-based broker who processed over $100m in crypto payments for Iranian oil sales since 2023. No new tranche has landed since Monday, but Treasury has said every country has been given a defined timeline, so further tranches should be treated as scheduled rather than speculative. This does not change any position or level; it is recorded as a standing headline risk that was not previously in the frame.
